about.title: Crescent City Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Crescent City is small enough that a sudden loss is felt well beyond one household. With roughly 6,800 residents, a death on US-101, along 5th Street or near L Street tends to touch neighbors, coworkers and the harbor community alike. In 2025, public records show 21 injury collisions and 32 people hurt here, with no traffic deaths recorded that year, yet wrongful death claims in Del Norte County arise from more than roadway crashes. Unsafe property, a workplace incident, a defective product or careless medical care can each leave a family carrying costs and an absence no one planned for. California allows a spouse or domestic partner and children, and in some cases other dependents or heirs, to bring a civil claim for funeral expenses, the income the person would have provided, and the love, companionship and guidance now missing. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. The service costs you nothing.

whyChoose.title: Why Del Norte County Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can sort out who in your family qualifies before any filing is made.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks considerably when a city, county or state agency is involved. Getting connected early keeps those dates from slipping past during a hard season.

items.title: Losses that reflect the whole person
items.desc: Recoverable damages go beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so pursuing the full claim does not require money up front.

items.question: If the death happened on US-101 near Crescent City, does that change the deadline?
items.answer: It can. Highway 101 through Del Norte County is maintained by a state agency, and claims against government entities in California generally require a formal notice within six months of the death, far sooner than the standard two-year limit. If a road condition, city vehicle or county employee may have played a role, mention it right away so the attorney can act on the shorter timeline.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves separately from any criminal prosecution in Del Norte County Superior Court. The two cases have different standards of proof, and a criminal acquittal does not prevent a civil claim from going forward. Many families begin the civil process while the criminal case is still pending.

items.question: What does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we connect you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency. That means the attorney is paid only if there is a recovery, and there is no charge to you for the introduction.
